review.headline: The Commissioner Finally Did It (And We Have Questions)
review.deck: Fourteen teams, a $200 auction, a thousand FAAB dollars each, an injury apocalypse, and a final standings page that reads like a police report. This is the official record of the 2025 season. Nobody comes out clean.

podium.note: The man who runs the league won the league. He has been commissioner here for the better part of a decade — he writes the rules, he approves the trades, he sets the FAAB budgets — and the year he finally lifts the trophy, the investigation is being conducted by him. Worse: he did it by being cheap. His auction board is the most boring document ever produced by this league. Biggest buy: $36 Ladd McConkey. Not one player over $40. James Cook at $31, Jalen Hurts at $22. While the rest of the league lit $60 bills on fire he clipped coupons, and it worked, which is the most insulting part. Fitting for a guy who works at Coinbase: he has watched enough people go all-in at the top to know exactly what that looks like, and he simply declined. Then he renamed the team from Hail Mary to Hail Purdy mid-glow-up. The audit is ongoing and the auditor is unavailable for comment.

Paid $56 for Jahmyr Gibbs, $49 for Puka Nacua, burned his FAAB to an even $0, dragged himself into the final — and lost it. Then he built this entire website, which means he has commissioned, designed, and personally deployed a permanent public monument to his own second-place finish. He wrote the code that renders this sentence. Respect. Also: therapy.

The team is called Shut Up because that is what this league has been saying to him since roughly 2013. It has never worked. He talks through the draft, he talks through the trade deadline, he talks through other people's matchups, and in 2025 he backed all of it up: 1,941.94 points, most in the league by a comfortable margin, tied for the best record at 22-6, Amon-Ra at $51 and a $44 Jonathan Taylor that printed all year. And he finished third. The best team in the league got clipped in the bracket and had to win the bronze game out of spite. He also ended the year with $940 of his $1,000 FAAB untouched, which is exactly what you would expect from a dentist: aggressive verbally, conservative with the drill. He talked more than anyone and has the least to show for it.

toilet.note: The Sacco does not go to the worst record. It goes to whoever loses the Sacco Bowl, and Greg lost it in the least defensible way this league has ever produced. He drew the 12 seed, lost the week-15 play-in to Poop Squad 108.76 to 142.84, and dropped into the bowl against a Leo the Cleo team that had already gone 4-24 and stopped opening the app. Two weeks. One job: outscore a corpse. He posted 106.68, then 74.22 — 180.90 total — while the corpse put up 234.22 on autopilot. He lost both weeks. He lost to a roster that was not being managed by a living person. This is a man who once played poker for a living, which means he has personally calculated worse odds than these and still found a way to be on the wrong side of them. It is engraved. There are no appeals.

story: Start with the money, because this league is constitutionally incapable of handling it. Fourteen $200 auction budgets went to war on draft night and the receipts are damning. The five biggest buys in league history all happened in one room on one night: $70 Ja'Marr Chase, $66 Bijan Robinson, $62 Saquon Barkley, $60 Justin Jefferson, $59 CeeDee Lamb. Combined final standing of those five owners: 6th, 14th, 8-20, 4th, and the Sacco. Not one of them reached the final. Meanwhile the commissioner quietly assembled a roster of $30 misfits and won the whole thing. The market was inefficient and Andrew was the only person in the room who read the prospectus.

Then October arrived and started collecting knees. Tyreek Hill's ACL detonated in Week 4 and took $30 of Bullish with it. Malik Nabers went down shortly after — $49 of Bend The Knee's budget, on a team named Bend The Knee, which is the kind of thing that would get flagged as too on-the-nose in a screenplay. Joe Burrow's toe ended Kim Jong Nate's $18 lottery ticket and simultaneously kneecapped the value of that $70 Chase, meaning one man's toe cost two different teams a season. Half of this league's draft capital was in a hospital by Halloween. And The Injured Reserved — a franchise named, years ago, for this exact scenario — went 21-7. You cannot write this. Somebody already did.

The regular season belonged to Neil, loudly. Most points in the league. Tied for the best record. He told everyone about it in real time, weekly, unprompted. And then the fantasy playoffs did what fantasy playoffs do, which is walk into a room and start swinging: the best team in the league got clipped before the final, won the third-place game out of pure spite, and left. He is now gone from the league entirely, which means the single loudest voice in fourteen years exits with zero rings and the most points ever scored in a season by somebody who did not win it. The silence is going to be strange.

Spare a thought for The Injured Reserved, who went 21-7, scored the third-most points in the league, allowed the fewest points of anybody, and finished fifth. That is a team that did every single thing correctly and got handed a consolation bracket for it. Greg lost one week and the bracket decided that was his personality now.

The luck ledger is uglier still. Bend The Knee went 10-18 while absorbing 1,788.8 points against — the most anyone was asked to survive all season. Kim Jong Nate outscored his opponents on the year and went 12-16 anyway, which is statistically closer to a curse than a season. Somewhere in this league there is a man who has never once been matched up against a team on a bye week and he does not know how good he has it.

Then there is the roster-move economy, where two philosophies were tested to destruction. FreeGucci made 66 transactions — the most in the league, more than one per day of the season — and finished 9th. Bullish made 12. Twelve. All year. A man named Bullish held his position through an eight-win season without so much as a stop loss, and finished 8-20. And Leo the Cleo made 53 moves on his way to 4-24, which is not roster management, that is pacing.

The final itself was Andrew's spreadsheet against Abhishek's stars, and the spreadsheet won 126.58 to 114.56. Sit with the arithmetic: the champion's most expensive player cost $36. Leo the Cleo's THIRD most expensive player cost more than that. The man who won this league did not own a single player anyone would have traded for, and that is either the most impressive drafting in league history or proof that none of us know anything, and honestly it can be both.

And at the bottom, the only genuinely dramatic finish of the year. The Sacco Bowl produced actual theatre: Greg lost the week-15 play-in, drew a 4-24 team for the final, needed to outscore a roster nobody was managing over two weeks, and lost both of them. The Sacco was contested this year. He won it fair and square. It has been engraved.

draft.intro: The 2025 auction, graded with the benefit of hindsight and zero mercy. $200 budgets, 16 roster spots, and some decisions that should have required a co-signer.

rows.verdict: No buy over $36 and a ring. Extreme couponing as a championship strategy.
Two anchors, real value underneath. Docked half a grade for how the story ends.
Best board in the league. The $44 Jonathan Taylor alone should hang in a museum. Didn't even need his whole wallet.
Paid full sticker for Jefferson and got exactly what the sticker said.
No star cost more than $40 and the team went 21-7. All floor, no ceiling, no shame.
$70 is a car payment. Then Cincinnati's quarterback situation happened to it.
Elite QB, big-money rookie, .500 record. Left $6 unspent, which is somehow the most on-brand detail.
Lamar at $32 was theft. The rest of the board was community service.
The Burrow ticket was voided by a toe. $55 CMC in 2025 was a faith-based initiative.
$59 CeeDee and the league's LOWEST points-for. That takes coordination.
$49 on Nabers' knee ligaments. The team name was a warning label.
$92 of it was gone by Halloween — Tyreek's knee and Saquon's regression. A margin call in jersey form.
Paid WR1 money for Brian Thomas Jr.'s gap year. The team name self-reported.
Rostered the best RB season money could buy and won four games. Under league review for Bijan neglect.

farewells.headline: The Departed: A Roasting Toast
farewells.intro: Two chairs empty out this season. League bylaws require they be roasted on the way through the door. Raise a glass.

people.name: Neil
people.title: The Dentist
people.toast: Neil leaves the way he arrived: mid-sentence. The team has been called Shut Up for over a decade because that is the single most common thing said to him in this league, and in fourteen years it has never landed once. He talked through drafts. He talked through other people's matchups. He explained your own roster to you. And the maddening part is that in 2025 he was right about all of it — 1,941 points, most in the league, 22-6, and a bronze medal for his trouble. The first recorded case of a dentist getting drilled. He exits with $940 of FAAB unspent, because of course the dentist left with the healthiest budget in league history: never touched, twice-a-year checkups only. Somewhere there is a waiver wire he told to rinse. The league loses its cleanest operator and its loudest man in a single chair, and the group chat is about to get very quiet in a way nobody is going to admit they miss. To Neil — may your new league appreciate 1,941 points more than we did, and may you finally extract the one thing you could not get here: a ring. And a word in edgewise.

people.name: Mohsin
people.title: The Bear In Bull's Clothing
people.toast: Mohsin named his team Bullish and then delivered the single most bearish season in franchise history: 8-20, a $62 Saquon that regressed, a $30 Tyreek whose knee filed for bankruptcy in Week 4, and a portfolio that got margin-called before the bye weeks. Then he made twelve roster moves. Twelve. All season. The man was long optimism and short results for a decade — every August he announced the bottom was in, every December he WAS the bottom — and when it all went wrong he refused to sell a single position, because that is not a strategy, that is a personality. He leaves as the league's greatest contrarian indicator and the all-time Sacco leader with three: 2016, 2018, 2022. Nobody else has more than one. To Mohsin — genuinely one of the great ones, a man who stayed bullish through eight separate bear markets of his own creation. The ticker is retired. Position closed. We are all short without you.

arrivals.headline: The Replacements: Jon & Tom
arrivals.body: In exchange for Mohsin and Neil, the league welcomes Jon Gragg and Tom Alshouse — and we need to be honest about the transaction that just occurred. Two brown guys out. Two white guys in. Straight swap, no picks, no protection. Jon and Tom. JON. AND. TOM. You cannot draft two whiter names; these are not fantasy managers, these are the guys who approve your mortgage. The seasoning cabinet has been consolidated into a single jar of mayonnaise and the group chat's median hot-sauce tolerance fell forty points overnight. And it has consequences beyond the chat. Every Thanksgiving this league watches Cowboys vs. Indians and it has always been a fair fight, because the Cowboys side historically ran a couple of Asians. Not anymore. As of this offseason the Cowboys are, demographically, cowboys. Actual cowboys. The Indians lost two starters in free agency and got nothing back. This is now the least competitive rivalry in American sport and it happens in Abhishek's living room every November. The credentials, briefly. Jon does analytics for FanDuel, which means he has spent a decade being paid to study degenerate behavior and has now, voluntarily, moved into the enclosure. He does not need to ask how your season is going. He can see it. He knows which one of us takes the Thursday night parlay at 11:40pm and he has known for years. Welcome to the study, Jon — you are also a subject now. Tom sells hard cider, a beverage with no natural enemies because nothing has ever actively chosen it. It is what you order when the bar is out of everything and you are not brave enough to say you do not like beer. Fourteen men who spend September screaming about running backs now have a dedicated apple juice supplier. The league has never been more hydrated or less intimidating. Welcome, gentlemen. You have inherited a $1,000 FAAB budget, a full-savage roast column, and a Thanksgiving tradition that is now a war crime. Draft accordingly.

worst_record.note: Four wins. FOUR. With $66 Bijan Robinson — the best running back purchase available to humanity — on the roster the entire time. That is being handed the keys to a Ferrari and reversing it into a lake. He owns the worst record in the fifteen-year database and still did not take the Sacco home, because when it finally mattered he outscored Greg by 53 points across two weeks without appearing to try. The only man in league history to lose 24 games and win something.

sacco_rules.headline: The Sacco Bowl
sacco_rules.body: Last place does not take the Sacco. The Sacco Bowl does. In playoff week one the 12 seed plays the 13 seed and the loser drops into the bowl; over the next two weeks that loser plays the 14 seed, and the lower two-week total takes it home. You can finish 10th and still win it. Ask Greg.
sacco_rules.footnote: Yahoo tracks none of this — it drops the bottom two seeds out of every bracket and forgets them — so every Sacco on this site was replayed from the weekly lineup scores on each team's public page. 2025 is confirmed. Earlier years are reconstructions under the same rule; if the league remembers one differently, the league is right.
